Cross-polytope.question: The _____ was Regular polytope dual to the hypercube in any number of dimensions.
Cross-polytope.fact: In geometry, a cross-polytope, hyperoctahedron, orthoplex, staurotope, or cocube is a regular, convex polytope that exists in n-dimensional Euclidean space. Cross-polytope.subject: Computer & IT
Cross-polytope.question: A second projection takes the _____(n−1)-gon petrie polygon of the lower dimension, seen as a bipyramid, projected down the axis, with 2 vertices mapped into the center
Cross-polytope.fact: The number of k-dimensional components (vertices, edges, faces, ..., facets) in an n-dimensional cross-polytope is thus given by (see binomial coefficient): 2 k + 1 ( n k + 1 ) {\displaystyle 2^{k+1}{n \choose {k+1}}} The extended f-vector for an n-orthoplex can be computed by (1,2)n, like the coefficients of polynomial products. There are many possible orthographic projections that can show the cross-polytopes as 2-dimensional graphs.
